transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-30 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lina (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood CSM), Priya (Aurora Head of ML), Ben (Aurora Infra), Aisha (Aurora Security), Tom (Aurora PM)

Summary (auto): Quick alignment on POC goals, scope of benchmarks, timeline, and deliverables. Plan: 3-week POC with kickoff, access setup, 1-week benchmark, mid-point tuning, exec readout.

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick roll call?
[00:10] Priya: Hey, Priya here, head of ML at Aurora.
[00:13] Ben: Ben, infra.
[00:14] Aisha: Aisha, security.
[00:16] Tom: Tom, product.
[00:18] Lina: Lina from Redwood, I'll lead the technical bits.
[00:20] Marcus: Marcus, CSM.
[00:22] Samir: Great. The goal today is to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and the timeline/milestones for the POC. We usually do a short kickoff, set up access, run benchmarks, do a midpoint review, then an exec readout. Any additions?
[00:35] Priya: That sounds good. Our big ask is we need to validate both latency and cost for our chat workflow and also ensure data residency and encryption controls.
[00:45] Lina: OK good. Can you tell us the workload shape? token sizes, concurrency, QPS?
[00:50] Tom: The real workload is a mix: typical user session averages ~300 tokens per request, but we have a tail to 1k on longer contexts. Concurrent active sessions we expect ~40-60 during peak, planned to scale later. We can provide a replay of production traffic.
[01:10] Ben: For baseline infra, we want to test on both hosted Redwood and also on a private VPC deployment to see diff in egress and latency.
[01:20] Aisha: Security checklist: we need SOC2 attestation, KMS integration for key management, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and audit logs. Also, we need to confirm no PII leaves our region.
[01:35] Samir: Got it. For the POC we'll scope two tracks: 1) Hosted Redwood API with dedicated capacity reserved for your tests, and 2) Private deployment in your VPC (lightweight package) for a subset of tests that require data controls.
[01:50] Priya: Timeline idea? We were hoping to move quickly — two to three weeks ideally.
[01:55] Lina: We typically do 3 weeks end-to-end: Week 0 kickoff + access, Week 1 run baseline benchmarks, Week 2 tuning and midpoint review, final few days exec readout and doc handoff. We can compress if needed but prefer 3 weeks to gather stable metrics.
[02:15] Tom: Sounds fine. What's the exact milestone list?
[02:18] Marcus: I'll outline: Kickoff (day 0) - align on requirements, share runbook. Access setup (day 1-3) - S3 sample data, API keys, VPC peering if needed. Benchmark run (day 4-10) - run load tests and quality evals. Midpoint review (end of week 2) - results and tuning. Exec readout + closeout (week 3).
[02:40] Priya: Success criteria: latency SLOs (95th < 250ms for 512 tokens), throughput target (sustain 60 concurrent sessions with p50 < 120ms), cost target (<= $X per 1M tokens, placeholder), and quality parity (no regression vs our current model on the set of 5 eval prompts).
[03:05] Lina: We'll capture those as measurable metrics. For quality parity, can you share eval prompts and golden outputs?
[03:12] Priya: Yes, we'll share a small evaluation suite, probably 50 prompts with labels.
[03:17] Ben: On access, we need instructions for VPC peering and also to understand what ports and IPs Redwood uses. Also KMS integration: does Redwood bring key material or do we keep it in our HSM?
[03:30] Samir: For KMS you can keep keys on your side, we support customer-managed keys and will walk through the KMS/HSM integration. For VPC peering we'll share a runbook. Lina will send network details.
[03:45] Aisha: We also need an NDA addendum and a short security questionnaire.
[03:48] Samir: Noted — I'll attach the security pack.
[03:50] 
[04:00] Lina: On benchmarks: recommended tests are latency distribution for 256/512/1024 token requests, sustained throughput test at target concurrency, cold-start and warm-path token throughput (KV cache behavior), and cost-per-token measurement. We'll also run a small quality regression suite. We'll provide load scripts and a detailed checklist.
[04:25] Priya: For the KV cache thing — can you explain what you mean? Our infra folks call it KV cache but docs mention K-V cash sometimes, so just want to be sure.
[04:33] Lina: Sorry, yes KV cache — the key-value cache of past tokens. We'll measure warm-start performance where cache hits reduce latency.
[04:40] Ben: Important: network egress from the VPC test nodes needs to be measured. We see differences in latency when traffic leaves the region.
[04:48] Samir: We'll run both in-region and cross-region variants and annotate results.
[04:54] Tom: Benchmarks — what's the minimum artifact you need from our side to start?
[04:58] Lina: Sample workload (replay), eval prompts, and access creds (S3 read, IAM role, or API key) plus a point person for networking.
[05:10] Ben: We can prep a 48-hour snapshot of production traffic for replay — will that be sufficient?
[05:15] Lina: Yes, and we'll guide how to anonymize PII. We'll also accept synthetic data if you prefer.
[05:22] Priya: On reporting, we want a concise dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost per 1M tokens, throughput, and quality score.
[05:30] Marcus: Redwood console will provide token-level cost and latency breakdowns; Lina will also provide a shared spreadsheet with raw results.
[05:36] Aisha: For compliance signoff, timeline wise, we need to review audit logs and KMS integration before exec readout. That may be a gating item.
[05:45] Samir: Agreed — we'll treat compliance validation as a gate before the exec meeting. If any blockers, we'll surface them at midpoint review.
[05:53] 
[06:00] Lina: Quick note on model variants — we recommend testing both a quantized 4-bit variant for cost and a 8-bit or fp16 for baseline latency. That way you can see the cost/quality tradeoff.
[06:12] Priya: Sounds good. We'll want to know how model rollbacks/fallbacks behave if capacity is hit.
[06:18] Lina: Redwood has smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible variants — we'll include that in the runbook and show results.
[06:25] Tom: Exec readout format? 20-30 minute summary with top metrics and recommended next steps?
[06:30] Marcus: Yes — we usually do a 20-min exec summary plus a brief demo of Redwood console and key charts.
[06:36] Priya: Can we get a pricing estimate for the POC and for ramping to production?
[06:40] Samir: I'll send a POC pricing sheet with dedicated capacity rates and options for reserved capacity.
[06:45] Aisha: Also send the security pack and SOC2 snapshot.
[06:48] Samir: Will do.
[06:50] 
[06:55] Action recap: Samir to send plan + price, Lina to share benchmark runbook and scripts, Aurora to provide sample dataset and network contact, Marcus to schedule kickoff and midpoint meetings.
[07:10] Tom: One quick question: what's the expected duration of the exec readout after the midpoint? Do we need to extend the POC if tuning takes longer?
[07:18] Lina: We build in two extra days for tuning post-midpoint. If more adjustments needed we'll discuss an extension — but 3-week is the target.
[07:26] Priya: That works. Thanks everyone.
[07:28] Samir: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the doc pack and dates.
[07:32] Meeting end.

References mentioned during call: Redwood POC runbook (link shared in chat), Benchmark checklist (to be shared), Security pack and SOC2 PDF (Samir to attach).
